title: Key resilience & TTL harmonizer: staged optimizer and rollback safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build an automated, low-risk service that proposes and applies per-prefix TTL and cache-key modifications (the "TTL Harmonizer") to reduce token-serving cost while maintaining SLOs. This ticket covers the model + offline simulation, the staged apply flow (shadow -> canary -> progressive), and circuit-breaker rollback rules for production. The scope excludes UI work (separate PM ticket) and kernel-level runtime changes; we will integrate with the existing runtime config API and rollout hooks.
acceptance_criteria: A predictive hit-rate model that consumes 7d production traces and outputs expected delta in hit-rate for a proposed TTL change per prefix
A simulation harness that replays historical traffic with candidate TTLs and reports expected backend QPS, per-prefix hit-rate, P95 latency delta, and cost delta
A staged apply pipeline: shadow apply -> 1% canary -> 10% progressive -> 100% rollout with automated health checks and rollback
Safety gates implemented: automatic rollback if backend load increases > 12% or P95 increases > 20% or user-facing error rate increases > 0.25%
Audit log entry for every apply and rollback including input proposal, simulation snapshot, metrics at each stage, and PR link
tasks: Design hit-rate model features (prefix popularity, sequence-length bucket, temporal decay, batching interaction) — Miguel + Research
Implement simulation harness using production trace replay (shadowing KV lookup decisions) — Eng-Infra
Add rollout orchestrator that calls runtime config API and monitors metrics via Console ingestion — Backend Team
Define canary cohorts and traffic steering rules (1% random, geolocation/tenant cohorts) — SRE
Implement circuit-breaker detector and automatic rollback controller — Reliability
Create runbook for manual override and postmortem steps — Ops
Add column-level audit events to audit log and wire to ElasticSearch and retention policy — Compliance
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after cost review flagged prefix hit-rate variance as a top-3 cost driver. Initial brainstorming with PM and Research (Aisha, Miguel, Priya).

2026-03-03: Research prototyped a simple hit-rate estimator using exponential decay over 7d windows and sequence-length segmentation; early results show ~8% cost reduction potential on a mid-tier workload when increasing TTLs for 12% of prefixes.
2026-03-05: Decided to prioritize safety: simulation before any production apply. Agreed on rollback thresholds above. Assigned canary cohorts to SRE (1% random followed by tenant-targeted 10%).

2026-03-08: Proof-of-concept simulation harness completed (shadow replay path integrated with request trace sink). Miguel ran initial dry-run against last 14 days and produced expected backend QPS profiles. Linked artifacts below.
2026-03-10: Implementation kickoff: infra engineers starting the rollout orchestrator. SRE to provide monitoring queries and alert rules by 2026-03-17.
notes: Tradeoffs considered: longer TTLs reduce egress and model compute but can increase stale outputs for dynamic user state; we bias proposals towards prefixes with historically idempotent outputs (embed/query fingerprints) and low content drift.

Cache-key stability: harmonizer will propose normalization rules (strip volatile suffixes, canonicalize timestamps) only after collision analysis via the simulation harness. Any proposed canonicalization must include a map of examples where normalization changes key counts.
Batching interaction: model defends against increased per-request token length changing batching behavior — simulation reports sequence-length distribution and expected batching latency impact.

Economic guardrails: a proposal that yields <2% cost improvement but increases operational risk will be deprioritized; threshold for auto-apply is currently >=3% expected cost reduction and no predicted SLO regressions.
Observability: the rollout orchestrator will publish a per-prefix rollout wire metric so we can compute attribution during partial rollouts. This avoids correlated-noise across prefixes.
